There's no practical limit in Thunderbird... but there probably is with your email provider. For example, Gmail has this to say,

https://support.google.com/mail/answer/22839

"You may see this message if you send an email to a total of more than 500 recipients in a single email and or more than 500 emails sent in a day. When you get this error, you should be able to send emails again within 1 to 24 hours."

If you do decide to send such a mass mailing you would be best off using Thunderbird's Mailing List feature.

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-create-and-use-mailing-lists-thunderbird

content: Migration of your Thunderbird data from the old Mac to the new Mac can be done with simple copy and drag & drop actions. On your old Mac copy the entire folder "Thunderbird" from your user Library on an external hard drive with at least 250 GB memory. Plug the external HD to your new Mac, verify that Thunderbird is not running, open a Finder window, select your user Library and drag & drop the Thunderbird folder in your user Library. If you have already run Thunderbird on the new Mac the system will ask you to replace the already existing Thunderbird folder.
